text:
Victor Mancini came to Vancouver from the Rangers in the J.T. Miller trade, a fifth-round pick out of Nebraska-Omaha who had already reached the NHL. This season he's been in and out (The Hockey News' lineup notes had him drawing in against Anaheim on Nov. 3), with eight games, no points and about 12 minutes a night.

The five-on-five numbers are rough: the Canucks get 36% of the shot attempts and 39% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on the ice. But that's only slightly worse than the team without him, and Vancouver has won one of the eight games he's played. The Canucks have also scored three fewer goals than their chances deserved during his shifts, which is finishing luck around him more than anything he controls.

Last season's context cuts both ways. Evolving-Hockey had his teammates among the weakest any defenseman played with (bottom 4%), which drags raw numbers down, but still had opponents creating more with him out there (bottom 2%), over a small 330 minutes. At 24, the right-shot, 229-pound Mancini has time. We'd watch whether his chances against settle once the team around him does.
headline: Victor Mancini and a blue line under water
